title: Flu Shot in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The RKI window is October to mid-December**, and a flu shot needs **10 to 14 days** before it protects you, so the date that matters is two weeks after your appointment.

**Berlin’s last four flu waves peaked on four different dates**: the week of 12 December 2022, 5 February 2024, 27 January 2025 and 19 January 2026. Only lab-confirmed cases are counted, but the timing is clear.

**A shot in the week of 2 November would have covered at least 95% of the Berlin cases in all four winters.** Two weeks later the early 2022/23 wave had already slipped to 86%, and a shot in the week of 7 December would have missed two thirds of it.

**The STIKO recommends it for everyone 60 and over**, pregnant women from the second trimester, people with chronic conditions, care-home residents, household contacts of people at risk and medical staff. Over 60 it should be a **high-dose or adjuvanted** vaccine.

**If you are in one of those groups, your statutory health insurance pays.** Under 60 without a reason it depends on your fund: many pay anyway, some only on reimbursement or with a doctor’s note, so ask before the appointment rather than after.
**Pharmacies can give the flu shot to adults 18 and over.** Walk-in slots are common in October and November, which is the easiest way round a GP who is booked out.
**People 60 and over made up 46% of Berlin’s lab-confirmed flu cases in 2025/26**, up from 18% in 2022/23, which is the plainest local argument for not skipping it once you are in that group.
